king-vasabha.name: King Vasabha
king-vasabha.summary: King Vasabha is regarded as a powerful ruler of Anuradhapura and the founder of the First Lambakanna Dynasty. According to the Mahavamsa, he defeated Subharaja and ruled for forty-four years. His reign is particularly associated with reservoirs, canals, urban defence, subterranean water channels and Buddhist patronage.
king-vasabha.biography:
King Vasabha made major contributions to the political, agricultural, urban and religious development of the Anuradhapura Kingdom.

According to the Mahavamsa, Vasabha belonged to the Lambakanna clan and served under his uncle, a military commander in the northern region. During the reign of Subharaja, a prophecy spread that a man named Vasabha would become king. Fearing this, Subharaja ordered that all persons bearing the name be killed. Vasabha's uncle decided to surrender him, but his uncle's wife Pottha secretly helped Vasabha escape by giving him money and warning him of the danger.

Vasabha fled to the Mahavihara, where the monks gave him food, milk and clothing. He then travelled village by village to Rohana, where over approximately two years he organised an army and built political support. He marched to Anuradhapura, defeated Subharaja in battle and gained the throne. He raised Pottha to the position of queen.

During his forty-four-year reign, Vasabha constructed twelve reservoirs and twelve canals, strengthened the city wall of Anuradhapura, built defensive towers at the four city gates, constructed a royal palace and royal garden tank, and developed bathing ponds supplied by subterranean water channels. He also provided extensive Buddhist patronage, building monasteries, stupas, chapter houses and image houses, and conducted the Vesak festival each year of his reign.
importantEvents: Defeated Subharaja and ascended the throne (c. 67 CE)
Constructed twelve reservoirs and twelve canals
Strengthened the city wall and built defensive towers at the four gates of Anuradhapura
Built a royal palace and subterranean water channels
Provided extensive Buddhist patronage across monasteries, stupas and image houses
Raised Pottha as queen after she helped him escape
constructions: Alisara Canal (with water share granted to Mucela Vihara)
City wall of Anuradhapura (raised and strengthened)
Defensive towers at the four city gates
Bathing ponds with subterranean supply channels
Image house at the Sacred Bodhi Tree

king-vankanasika-tissa.name: King Vankanasika Tissa
king-vankanasika-tissa.summary: King Vankanasika Tissa succeeded King Vasabha as ruler of the Anuradhapura Kingdom.
king-vankanasika-tissa.biography: King Vankanasika Tissa was a ruler of the Anuradhapura Kingdom. Traditional sources identify him as the son of King Vasabha. He was succeeded by King Gajabahu I.
importantEvents: Belonged to the First Lambakanna Dynasty
Traditionally identified as the father of King Gajabahu I

king-gajabahu-i.name: King Gajabahu I
king-gajabahu-i.summary: King Gajabahu I succeeded King Vankanasika Tissa.
king-gajabahu-i.biography: King Gajabahu I was a ruler of the Anuradhapura Kingdom. He is traditionally identified as the son of King Vankanasika Tissa and is remembered as an important ruler in Sri Lankan chronicles and later traditions.
